name: Neo4j
one_liner: Graph database with a REST Aura management API, an HTTP Query API for Cypher, drivers, and an official local MCP server.
auth_notes: Aura management API: OAuth2 client_credentials (client ID/secret from console) yielding a bearer token. Query API and drivers authenticate to a database instance with database user credentials (HTTP Basic). Basic for Query API inferred, not quoted.
access_notes: Aura API credentials self-serve in console for all tiers; AuraDB Free (one instance per account) exists. Aura API limit 25 req/min for Free/unbilled trials, 125 req/min for paid tiers. Query API works against any instance, incl. self-managed.

buildability.rationale: Both Aura management API (self-serve OAuth client credentials) and Query API (per-instance Cypher over HTTP) are documented and self-serve. Choose target: instance lifecycle vs data access; endpoint count unverified and Free tier is rate limited.

needs_human_reason: Must decide whether the target is the Aura management API or per-instance Query API/Cypher; Aura endpoint list is in a JS-rendered spec not fetched.

access.quote: AuraDB Free and AuraDB Professional trial accounts without a billing method attached, get a rate limit of 25 requests per minute.
You can only create one Free instance per account.

api_surface.quote: The Aura API allows you to programmatically perform actions on your Aura instances without the need to log in to the Console.
The Query API allows to execute Cypher statements against a Neo4j server through HTTP requests.

mcp.quote: The official MCP Server for Neo4j, is a local MCP server that is downloadable as a binary
Neo4j MCP gives AI assistants and LLM-powered tools direct, structured access to your Neo4j graph database.

disputes.why: Aura API and Query API are both HTTP APIs; Query API executes Cypher over HTTP.
Per-instance Query API needs database credentials in addition to Aura OAuth client credentials.
Aura API overview documents 25 and 125 req/min tiers.
Aura management API vs Query API/drivers target remains the real decision.
Vendor GitHub repo is the canonical official source; PyPI is a package mirror. MCP is local, not hosted.
AuraDB Free instance and local self-managed installs available for testing.
